item.title: Inside Vance’s Iran negotiations: No deal, but ‘friendly’ talks
item.summary: Vice President JD Vance’s negotiations in Pakistan with Iran failed to end the war, but progress was reported on building goodwill.

item.title: Democrats say GOP broke promise on prices, but some swing voters lost faith in change
item.summary: President Donald Trump’s attack on Iran sent gas prices surging, giving Democrats’ focus on affordability more traction if they can get voters to trust them.

item.title: At a mahjong table in Iowa, a struggle over which party to trust
item.summary: Women courted in key races weigh their choices — and whether the president’s policies have delivered for a working-class town hit by tariffs, war and rising costs.

item.title: Vance, who wasn’t keen on Iran war, now tasked with trying to end it
item.summary: The weekend’s peace talks in Islamabad mark Vance’s highest-profile assignment as vice president, with concomitant political risk.

item.title: Trump announces naval blockade of Iran after Islamabad talks yield no deal
item.summary: The blockade could derail a tenuous ceasefire after just five days. Vice President JD Vance said the U.S. remains open to diplomacy if Iran takes “our final and best offer.”

item.title: Bust of multi-state drug ring highlights increasing use of police drones
item.summary: Once a novelty, drones are now being flown by more than 5,000 large and small law enforcement agencies across the nation.

item.title: Federal judges say White House ballroom construction can continue, for now
item.summary: President Donald Trump has claimed that halting the project poses a risk to national security and threatens him.

item.title: In 1990, a bipartisan Congress passed historic bills. Then it cracked apart.
item.summary: 36 years ago, a Republican president and Democratic lawmakers produced monumental laws. Now, a broken Congress has enabled Trump to undo key parts of that legacy.

item.title: Trump, sounding like Biden, says he deserves more credit
item.summary: America’s last two presidents have spent years as political foils. Both feel the American public does not give them enough credit.

item.title: Eric Swalwell, California governor candidate, accused of sexual assault by ex-staffer
item.summary: Supporters of Rep. Eric Swalwell’s campaign withdrew support, including two congressmen who chaired his campaign and two senators who endorsed his bid. Swalwell denied the allegations.
